Subject: Data use terms — no-train / proof-of-deletion / ingest options

Hi Tessa,

We're finalizing our DPA and need confirmation of a few items before procurement signs off. HealthNest's legal team is asking for: a) an enforceable no-model-improvement (no-train) commitment for tenant data, b) concrete evidence you can provide when data is deleted (time-stamped deletion reports, hashes, or similar), and c) clear options for ingestion that minimize training/exposure surface (we're evaluating an SFTP batch flow vs API with a no-train header).

Attached is our redline of the standard DPA with the no-train clause highlighted. Can Redwood:
- Confirm the exact controls you will use to honor a no-train request (how it's enforced in the runtime),
- Describe what a proof-of-deletion package looks like and whether you can export it, and
- Tell us pros/cons of SFTP batch ingestion vs API (we care about operational cadence, auditability, and data residency).

We also need confirmation of EU residency for processing. Procurement would like a draft SOW for an SFTP flow if that's an option.

Thanks — if possible we'd like a short write-up by next Wednesday so procurement can review.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Counsel, HealthNest

Hi Elena — thanks for sending the redline. We're able to support a firm no-model-improvement commitment for HealthNest tenant data and can provide audit-grade deletion evidence.

Quick answers up front:
- Enforcement: requests can be honored via a dedicated "no-train" routing flag that bypasses any model-improvement pipelines; we operate a separate non-learning runtime path (details below).
- Proof-of-deletion: we can export timestamped deletion reports, correlated audit logs, and a signed attestation document.
- Ingest options: both SFTP and API are viable. SFTP gives clearer batch boundaries and easier artifact retention/deletion proofs; API can be more real-time and supports an "x-no-train: true" header for per-request control.

I'm looping in our engineering and legal leads to provide a short technical/attestation write-up and a draft SOW for SFTP. Can you confirm the EU region requirement (single-country residency or EU-wide)? We'll target a response by next Wednesday afternoon PT.

—Tessa

Notes from engineering (high-level, customer-facing):

1) How "no-train" is enforced
- Architecture: We have an isolated non-learning inference path. Traffic marked with tenant flag (tenant config or request header) is routed to GPU pools with learning/telemetry hooks disabled. No records from that path feed into any model improvement pipelines.
- Runtime: KV caches are kept ephemeral per-request and are not persisted to S3 training buckets. Periodic cache scrub jobs run hourly; retention windows are logged.
- Headers/Flags: For API, we honor x-redwood-no-train: true. For SFTP, the ingestion manifest includes a metadata field enforce_no_train=true so files are processed into the non-learning pipeline.

2) Proof-of-deletion artifacts we can produce
- Deletion report: CSV with file/object ids, timestamps, deletion job id, operator id (or automation id).
- Audit slice: signed log export (gzipped) containing request ids, routing flags, and retention actions (we redact PII from logs but include hashed object ids).
- Attestation: generated PDF signed by our compliance team including the deletion job hash and timestamp.
- Cryptographic evidence: we can provide HMAC/SHA256 digests of object lists so HealthNest can verify deletion artifacts against their own inventory.

3) Caveats & embeddings
- Embeddings: we sometimes cache embeddings for latency. For no-train tenants we can either skip caching or keep encryption keys customer-specific and rotate/destroy keys on retention removal. If HealthNest wants no persistent embeddings, we recommend the SFTP batch flow where we can guarantee ephemeral processing with no indexing.

4) EU residency and SFTP
- We can host processing in an EU region (single-region pinning available). SFTP endpoints can be provisioned in the EU zone and storage buckets will be EU-only.

5) Operational notes for SFTP vs API (brief)
- SFTP: clearer boundaries, easier to provide deletion reports per-file, preferred when the customer wants batch control or strict residency. Slightly slower turnaround.
- API: lower latency, better for interactive features; requires careful per-request flagging and stronger real-time auditing.

If you want, I'll assemble a one-page technical appendix showing sample deletion-report CSV and log entry examples (no real PII) for the customer packet.

—Dev

Team — suggested language and evidence list below for inclusion in the customer packet / DPA addendum. Please treat this as customer-facing legal text (we can shorten for the packet):

Proposed clause (redline-ready):
"Provider shall not use Customer Data for the purpose of improving or training models, including transfer into model training corpora or supervised fine-tuning datasets (\"No-Model-Improvement\"). Provider will process Customer Data in an isolated non-learning runtime and will not persist Customer Data to model development or training stores. Provider will, upon Customer request, provide a Deletion Evidence Package as described below."

Deletion Evidence Package (we will deliver the following within 10 business days of a deletion request):
- Timestamped Deletion Report (CSV) that lists object identifiers and deletion job ids.
- Signed Audit Export (log slice) covering the affected objects and routing flags (we will redact PII while preserving hashed identifiers).
- Compliance Attestation (PDF) signed by Provider's compliance officer.
- Where applicable, cryptographic hashes of deleted object lists to enable Customer verification.

We should attach: the no-train attestation template, a sample deletion report (CSV), and a short FAQ describing what the audit export contains and how to verify hashes. I'll prepare the DPA addendum redline and seed a DocuSign envelope; attaching proposed DocuSign link. Aditya/Marissa — please draft an SOW for SFTP that includes EU-only endpoints, retention windows, and an acceptance test (prove deletion for a sample batch).

—Lauren
